v: In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month,[^1] the word of the LORD[^2] came through[^3] Haggai the prophet[^4] to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:[^5]

בִּשְׁנַ֤ת שְׁתַּ֙יִם֙ לְדָרְיָ֣וֶשׁ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֜ה בְּיַד־חַגַּ֣י הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל֙ פַּחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֧עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֛ק הַכֹּהֵ֥ן הַגָּד֖וֹל לֵאמֹֽר׃
This is what the LORD of Armies[^6] says: These people say, "The time has not come, the time for the house of the LORD to be rebuilt."
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א עֶת־בֹּ֛א עֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה לְהִבָּנֽוֹת׃ פ
Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:
וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה בְּיַד־חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses,[^7] while this house lies in ruins?
הַעֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אַתֶּ֔ם לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֣ם סְפוּנִ֑ים וְהַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה חָרֵֽב׃
Now this is what the LORD of Armies says: Consider your ways.[^8]
וְעַתָּ֕ה כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֖ם עַל־דַּרְכֵיכֶֽם׃

You have sown much, but harvested little. You eat, but never have enough; you drink, but never have your fill; you put on clothes, but no one is warm. And whoever earns wages earns them to put into a bag with holes.
זְרַעְתֶּ֨ם הַרְבֵּ֜ה וְהָבֵ֣א מְעָ֗ט אָכ֤וֹל וְאֵין־לְשָׂבְעָה֙ שָׁת֣וֹ וְאֵין־לְשָׁכְרָ֔ה לָב֖וֹשׁ וְאֵין־לְחֹ֣ם ל֑וֹ וְהַ֨מִּשְׂתַּכֵּ֔ר מִשְׂתַּכֵּ֖ר אֶל־צְר֥וֹר נָקֽוּב׃ פ
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Consider your ways.
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶ֖ם עַל־דַּרְכֵיכֶֽם׃
Go up into the hills, bring wood and build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be honored,[^9] says the LORD.
עֲל֥וּ הָהָ֛ר וַהֲבֵאתֶ֥ם עֵ֖ץ וּבְנ֣וּ הַבָּ֑יִת וְאֶרְצֶה־בּ֥וֹ *ואכבד **וְאֶכָּבְדָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

You looked for much, but see, it came to little. When you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of Armies.[^10] Because of my house, which lies in ruins, while each of you runs off to his own house.
פָּנֹ֤ה אֶל־הַרְבֵּה֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה לִמְעָ֔ט וַהֲבֵאתֶ֥ם הַבַּ֖יִת וְנָפַ֣חְתִּי ב֑וֹ יַ֣עַן מֶ֗ה נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת יַ֗עַן בֵּיתִי֙ אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא חָרֵ֔ב וְאַתֶּ֥ם רָצִ֖ים אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃
Therefore, because of you, the heavens have held back the dew, and the earth has held back its produce.
עַל־כֵּ֣ן עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם כָּלְא֥וּ שָ[c]מַ֖יִם מִטָּ֑ל וְהָאָ֖רֶץ כָּלְאָ֥ה יְבוּלָֽהּ׃

I have called for a drought[^11] on the land and on the hills, on the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, on what the ground produces, on human beings and animals, and on all the work of your hands.

וָאֶקְרָ֨א חֹ֜רֶב עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ וְעַל־הֶהָרִ֗ים וְעַל־הַדָּגָן֙ וְעַל־הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְעַל־הַיִּצְהָ֔ר וְעַ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹצִ֖יא הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְעַל־הָֽאָדָם֙ וְעַל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל כָּל־יְגִ֥יעַ כַּפָּֽיִם׃ ס

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the rest of the people[^12] obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.

וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע זְרֻבָּבֶ֣ל ׀ בֶּֽן־שַׁלְתִּיאֵ֡ל וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָק֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְכֹ֣ל ׀ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית הָעָ֗ם בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וְעַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ חַגַּ֣י הַנָּבִ֔יא כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁלָח֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּֽירְא֥וּ הָעָ֖ם מִפְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
Then Haggai, the LORD's messenger,[^13] gave the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you, declares the LORD."
וַ֠יֹּאמֶר חַגַּ֞י מַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה בְּמַלְאֲכ֥וּת יְהוָ֖ה לָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲנִ֥י אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

So the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people. They came and began work on the house of the LORD of Armies, their God,

וַיָּ֣עַר יְהוָ֡ה אֶת־רוּחַ֩ זְרֻבָּבֶ֨ל בֶּן־שַׁלְתִּיאֵ֜ל פַּחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶת־ר֙וּחַ֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָק֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל וְֽאֶת־ר֔וּחַ כֹּ֖ל שְׁאֵרִ֣ית הָעָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ מְלָאכָ֔ה בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃ פ
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.[^14]
בְּי֨וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בַּשִּׁשִּׁ֑י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֥וֶשׁ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

n.1: Darius I, king of Persia (522–486 BC). The date is 29 August 520 BC. The months are counted from the spring, so the sixth month fell in August and September.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "by the hand of". Also in verses 3 and 13 and in 2:1.
n.4: Haggai and Zechariah urged the people of Judah to rebuild the temple (Ezra 5:1–2; 6:14). Exiles had returned from Babylon after 538 BC and laid the foundation of the temple, but the work had stopped (Ezra 3:8–13; 4:24). The name *Haggai* probably means "born on a festival".
n.5: Zerubbabel was a grandson of King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3:17–19). He was governor of the Persian province of Judah. Joshua, called Jeshua in Ezra 3:2, was the grandson of the last high priest before the exile (1 Chronicles 5:40–41, 6:14–15 in most English Bibles).
n.6: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. The title is used often in Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi.
n.7: Hebrew *sefunim*, "covered", that is, roofed or paneled with wood, as were the royal buildings (1 Kings 7:3, 7).
n.8: Literally "Set your heart on your ways". Also in verse 7.
n.10: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH tseva'ot*, "the declaration of the LORD of Armies", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. *Declares the LORD* is also in verse 13.
n.11: Hebrew *chorev*, "drought", which sounds like *charev*, "in ruins" (verses 4 and 9).
n.12: Literally "all the remnant of the people", those who had come back from the exile. Also in verse 14.
n.13: Hebrew *mal'akh*, "messenger", the word also used for an angel. Compare Malachi 3:1.

v: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month,[^1] the word of the LORD[^2] came through Haggai the prophet:
בַּשְּׁבִיעִ֕י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה בְּיַד־חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people, and say:
אֱמָר־נָ֗א אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־שַׁלְתִּיאֵל֙ פַּחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֑וֹל וְאֶל־שְׁאֵרִ֥ית הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?[^3] How does it look to you now? Does it not seem to you like nothing at all?
מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ הַנִּשְׁאָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאָה֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה בִּכְבוֹד֖וֹ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וּמָ֨ה אַתֶּ֜ם רֹאִ֤ים אֹתוֹ֙ עַ֔תָּה הֲל֥וֹא כָמֹ֛הוּ כְּאַ֖יִן בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD.[^4] Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,[^5] declares the LORD, and work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of Armies,[^6]

וְעַתָּ֣ה חֲזַ֣ק זְרֻבָּבֶ֣ל ׀ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֡ה וַחֲזַ֣ק יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָק֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וַחֲזַ֨ק כָּל־עַ֥ם הָאָ֛רֶץ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אִתְּכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
as I promised you[^7] when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit[^8] remains among you. Do not be afraid.
אֶֽת־הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־כָּרַ֤תִּי אִתְּכֶם֙ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֣ם מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְרוּחִ֖י עֹמֶ֣דֶת בְּתוֹכְכֶ֑ם אַל־תִּירָֽאוּ׃ ס
For this is what the LORD of Armies says: Once more, in a little while,[^9] I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת ע֥וֹד אַחַ֖ת מְעַ֣ט הִ֑יא וַאֲנִ֗י מַרְעִישׁ֙ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־הֶחָרָבָֽה׃
I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come,[^10] and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Armies.
וְהִרְעַשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֖אוּ חֶמְדַּ֣ת כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמִלֵּאתִ֞י אֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ כָּב֔וֹד אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of Armies.
לִ֥י הַכֶּ֖סֶף וְלִ֣י הַזָּהָ֑ב נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
The glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former,[^11] says the LORD of Armies. And in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of Armies.
גָּד֣וֹל יִֽהְיֶ֡ה כְּבוֹד֩ הַבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֤ה הָאַֽחֲרוֹן֙ מִן־הָ֣רִאשׁ֔וֹן אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וּבַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן שָׁל֔וֹם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius,[^12] the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet:
בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְאַרְבָּעָה֙ לַתְּשִׁיעִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Ask the priests for a ruling:[^13]
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שְׁאַל־נָ֧א אֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים תּוֹרָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
"If someone carries consecrated meat[^14] in the fold of his garment, and with the fold he touches bread or stew or wine or oil or any other food, does it become holy?" The priests answered, "No."

הֵ֣ן ׀ יִשָּׂא־אִ֨ישׁ בְּשַׂר־קֹ֜דֶשׁ בִּכְנַ֣ף בִּגְד֗וֹ וְנָגַ֣ע בִּ֠כְנָפוֹ אֶל־הַלֶּ֨חֶם וְאֶל־הַנָּזִ֜יד וְאֶל־הַיַּ֧יִן וְאֶל־שֶׁ֛מֶן וְאֶל־כָּל־מַאֲכָ֖ל הֲיִקְדָּ֑שׁ וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹֽא׃
Then Haggai said, "If someone who is unclean from contact with a dead body[^15] touches any of these, does it become unclean?" The priests answered, "It becomes unclean."
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חַגַּ֔י אִם־יִגַּ֧ע טְמֵא־נֶ֛פֶשׁ בְּכָל־אֵ֖לֶּה הֲיִטְמָ֑א וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יִטְמָֽא׃
Then Haggai answered, "So it is with this people, and so it is with this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so with all the work of their hands. Whatever they offer there is unclean.[^16]
וַיַּ֨עַן חַגַּ֜י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֵּ֣ן הָֽעָם־הַ֠זֶּה וְכֵן־הַגּ֨וֹי הַזֶּ֤ה לְפָנַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְכֵ֖ן כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַקְרִ֛יבוּ שָׁ֖ם טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃
Now consider[^17] from this day onward.[^18] Before stone was laid on stone in the temple of the LORD,
וְעַתָּה֙ שִֽׂימוּ־נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִטֶּ֧רֶם שֽׂוּם־אֶ֛בֶן אֶל־אֶ֖בֶן בְּהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃
how did you fare?[^19] When someone came to a heap of twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures from the press,[^20] there were only twenty.
מִֽהְיוֹתָ֥ם בָּא֙ אֶל־עֲרֵמַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה בָּ֣א אֶל־הַיֶּ֗קֶב לַחְשֹׂף֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים פּוּרָ֔ה וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִֽים׃
I struck you, all the work of your hands, with blight and mildew and hail, yet you did not turn to me,[^21] declares the LORD.
הִכֵּ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בַּשִּׁדָּפ֤וֹן וּבַיֵּֽרָקוֹן֙ וּבַבָּרָ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיכֶ֑ם וְאֵין־אֶתְכֶ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Consider from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day when the foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid. Consider:
שִׂימוּ־נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִיּוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַתְּשִׁיעִ֗י לְמִן־הַיּ֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יֻסַּ֥ד הֵֽיכַל־יְהוָ֖ה שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶֽם׃
Is there still seed in the barn? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not yet borne fruit.[^22] From this day on I will bless you."
הַע֤וֹד הַזֶּ֙רַע֙ בַּמְּגוּרָ֔ה וְעַד־הַגֶּ֨פֶן וְהַתְּאֵנָ֧ה וְהָרִמּ֛וֹן וְעֵ֥ץ הַזַּ֖יִת לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֑א מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲבָרֵֽךְ׃ ס
The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה ׀ שֵׁנִית֙ אֶל־חַגַּ֔י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר׃
Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am about to shake the heavens and the earth.
אֱמֹ֕ר אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֥ל פַּֽחַת־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲנִ֣י מַרְעִ֔ישׁ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

I will overturn[^23] the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his comrade.[^24]
וְהָֽפַכְתִּי֙ כִּסֵּ֣א מַמְלָכ֔וֹת וְהִ֨שְׁמַדְתִּ֔י חֹ֖זֶק מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְהָפַכְתִּ֤י מֶרְכָּבָה֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֶ֔יהָ וְיָרְד֤וּ סוּסִים֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ בְּחֶ֥רֶב אָחִֽיו׃

On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declares the LORD, and I will make you like a signet ring,[^25] for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of Armies.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֣וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֡וֹת אֶ֠קָּחֲךָ זְרֻבָּבֶ֨ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֤ל עַבְדִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ כַּֽחוֹתָ֑ם כִּֽי־בְךָ֣ בָחַ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

n.1: 17 October 520 BC, the last day of the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus 23:34–36).
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Solomon's temple, destroyed by the Babylonians in 587 or 586 BC, about sixty-six years before. Some of the older people had wept when the new foundation was laid (Ezra 3:12).
n.4: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.5: Hebrew *am ha-arets*, here the whole community in Judah.
n.6: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.7: Literally "the word that I cut with you", the language of making a covenant. The Septuagint does not have the first half of this verse.
n.9: Literally "Yet once, it is a little". Hebrews 12:26 quotes this verse from the Septuagint: "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven."
n.10: Hebrew *chemdat*, "what is desired, precious things". The verb is plural, which points to treasures (compare verse 8). Traditionally "the desire of all nations shall come", following the Latin Vulgate, which many Christian readers took as a title of the Messiah.
n.11: Or "The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former".
n.12: 18 December 520 BC. Also in verses 18 and 20.
n.13: Hebrew *torah*, here a priest's decision on a point of the law (Leviticus 10:10–11; Deuteronomy 17:11).
n.14: Literally "holy flesh", meat from a sacrifice. Whatever touched it became holy (Leviticus 6:20, 6:27 in most English Bibles), but holiness did not pass on any further.
n.15: Literally "one unclean of *nephesh*", that is, by contact with a dead person (Numbers 19:11–13, 22). Uncleanness spreads more easily than holiness.
n.16: *There* is probably the altar, rebuilt soon after the return (Ezra 3:2–3).
n.17: Literally "set your heart". Also in verse 18.
n.18: Or "think back from this day". The Hebrew phrase usually looks forward, but verses 15–17 recall the past.
n.19: Literally "since they were". The Septuagint reads "who were you?"
n.20: Hebrew *purah*, a vat or wine trough.
n.21: Literally "and there was nothing of you to me". The line echoes Amos 4:9, where the Hebrew is "you did not return to me".
n.22: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Or "Is the seed still in the barn? Have the vine … not yet borne fruit?"
n.23: Hebrew *hafakh*, the word used of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:25; Amos 4:11).
n.25: A ring with a seal, worn by a king or his officials as the sign of their authority. The LORD had said that he would pull off King Jehoiachin, Zerubbabel's grandfather, like a signet ring (Jeremiah 22:24). Zerubbabel is named in the genealogies of Jesus (Matthew 1:12–13; Luke 3:27).
